title: Isolation and feeder-free primary culture of four cell types from a single human skin sample
protocol: Decontaminate tissue culture hood.
Prepare vacuum aspirator by adding bleach; volume should be sufficient for decontaminating liquid waste if vessel is filled (approximately 10% final concentration).
Preheat glass bead sterilizer.
Prepare Dispase solution at a concentration of 2.4 U/mL in HBS; filter sterilize the solution and store frozen in aliquots (-20°C) until use.
Thaw Dispase at 37°C and store on ice until used in procedure.
Warm HBS in 37°C water bath prior to use.
Use freshly excised human skin as soon as possible for optimal results.
Store skin in a buffer solution at 4°C if immediate use is not possible, up to 1–2 hours.
Rinse skin thoroughly to remove blood before storing it in KGM at 4°C for up to 24 hours.
Trim excess subcutaneous tissue prior to overnight storage in KGM to improve preservation and cell viability.
Cut the skin to the desired size.
Remove any necrotic tissue if necessary.
Rinse the skin sample 2× with 20 mL HBS in a 100 mm dish.
Remove as much subcutaneous fat as possible.
Place the skin sample in a dish with the fat side facing up.
Add a small amount of HBS to the dish to prevent drying.
Grasp the fat with fine tip forceps and cut it away using curved scissors.
Discard the removed fat.
Observe that the dermis appears whitish after subcutaneous fat removal.
Set up 6 100 mm dishes in the hood: 2 containing 20 mL 5% Dettol, and 4 containing 20 mL HBS.
Wash the skin quickly (∼15 s) by placing it in a dish with 5% Dettol and manipulating the tissue using sterile forceps to expose all surfaces to Dettol.
Remove from Dettol and rinse the skin twice for about 30 s each in HBS by moving to fresh dishes, ensuring thorough manipulation of the skin at each rinse.
Repeat the Dettol and two HBS rinses with a new set of dishes as necessary.
Place the skin in a clean, sterile 100 mm dish with 10 mL HBS after the final rinse.
Aspirate to remove HBS and Dettol from used dishes, then discard the dishes.
Measure and record the area of the skin sample.
Place skin in a dish with approximately 10 mL HBS.
Cut the skin sample into strips measuring approximately 2 cm × 0.25 cm.
Clamp a Weck-prep blade in the teeth of a hemostat.
Position the blade edge on the skin, perpendicular to the surface, dermis side down.
Run a sterile scalpel blade along the edge of the razor blade to cut the strips.
Transfer tissue strips to a 100 mm dish containing 35 mL Dispase.
Place the dish into a zippered plastic bag.
Incubate overnight at 4°C.
If using split-thickness skin or very thin skin, place two layers of sterile cotton gauze in the dish and saturate with Dispase.
Lay the tissue strips on the gauze with dermis side down.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Check for separation of epidermis from dermis after 30 minutes.
If necessary, continue incubation at 37°C every 30 minutes up to 2 hours.
Once epidermis easily separates from dermis, immediately proceed to the next steps.
Prepare aspirator by adding bleach to achieve a 10% final concentration.
Decontaminate tissue culture hood.
Pre-heat glass bead sterilizer.
Turn on centrifuge and pre-cool to 4°C.
Prepare Trypsin/EDTA solution containing 0.025% Trypsin + 0.02% EDTA in HBS.
Filter sterilize the Trypsin/EDTA solution.
Store Trypsin/EDTA solution in aliquots at -20°C until use.
Thaw Trypsin/EDTA solution at 37°C for the minimum time required.
Store thawed Trypsin/EDTA solution on ice until needed.
Warm Trypsin/EDTA solution to 37°C immediately before use.
Store trypsin on ice after thawing and warming to 37°C for the minimum required time prior to use.
Weigh collagenase and store aliquots in snap-cap or screw-cap glass vials in a desiccator at 4°C.
Calculate the amount of collagenase (mg) needed per aliquot using the formula: 625 U/mL × mg enzyme activity (U) × 30 mL = # mg collagenase per vial.
Combine 28.5 mL KGM with 1.5 mL BPE in a 50 mL tube to prepare working collagenase solution.
Dissolve small amounts of collagenase from glass vial into the prepared buffer and bring volume to 30 mL.
Filter sterilize the collagenase solution using a 0.22 μm 50 mL tube-top filter.
Store the collagenase solution on ice until ready for use.
Warm FGM, “regular” calcium KGM, and ECGM to 37°C in a water bath before use, protecting from light.
Dilute the 100× Collagen I Solvent provided with the kit 1:100 with sterile Milli-Q water and store at 4°C.
To coat one T225 flask, dilute collagen I solution (1 mg/mL) 1:10 in 1× Collagen I Solvent and add 11.25 mL per flask (5 μg/cm²).
Incubate the coated flasks for a minimum of 1 h at 37°C.
Aspirate the collagen I solution from each flask.
Rinse each flask three times with 10 mL HBS.
Add 45 mL KGM to each flask and pre-equilibrate in an incubator at 37°C for at least 30 min if used immediately.
Air dry the flask in a hood and store at 4°C if not used immediately.
Prepare T150 flasks for fibroblast inoculation.
Add 10 mL FGM to each flask.
Equilibrate the flasks in the incubator for ≥30 minutes before use.
Prepare Attachment Factor-coated flask(s) according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Rock vigorously with 3–4 mL Attachment Factor to completely cover growth surface.
Incubate sealed flask at 37°C for 30 minutes or at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for ≥2 hours.
Aspirate liquid without rinsing and store the flask tightly capped in the hood at room temperature for up to 24 hours.
Add 15 mL ECGM per flask before use and equilibrate in the incubator for ≥30 minutes.
Prepare 100 mL KGM + 10% FBS and store on ice until ready to use.
Separate epidermis from dermis using scissors and place tissue strips in a 100 mm dish containing 10 mL HBS.
Place two additional 100 mm dishes with 20 mL HBS each, labeled for “epidermis” and “dermis”.
Separate dermis from epidermis.
Grasp the dermis with fine-tipped forceps.
Grasp the epidermis with blunt forceps.
Peel off the epidermis.
Place epidermal strips in a fresh dish labeled “epidermis”.
Add 20 mL HBS to the dish containing epidermal strips.
Store the dish with epidermal strips in a plastic zippered bag.
Keep the bag refrigerated or in a cold room at 4°C until processing for keratinocyte isolation.
Grasp each dermal strip at one end with forceps.
Use blunt forceps to squeeze the dermal strip near that end.
Run the blunt forceps down the length of the strip, squeezing gently, to extrude endothelial cells.
Repeat this procedure ten times for each dermal strip.
Transfer the treated dermal strip to a fresh dish containing 20 mL HBS labeled “dermis” for subsequent isolation of fibroblasts.
Transfer the extruded cell suspension to a sterile 50 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Rinse the dish used for extruding HDMEC several times with small amounts of ECGM and add to the conical tube.
Centrifuge the contents for 7 minutes at 1000 rpm (approximately 250×g) at 4°C without brake.
Aspirate or pipette off the supernatant carefully, avoiding the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 2 mL ECGM per T75 flask.
Inoculate prepared T75 flasks (coated with Attachment Factor and equilibrated with medium at 37°C) with 2 mL of the cell suspension per flask.
Incubate the inoculated flasks overnight (∼16 hours) at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Carefully remove HBS from the dish containing dermal strips using a 25 mL pipet and forceps to keep the dermal strips away from the pipet.
Mince the dermis into small pieces (<0.5–1 mm3) using a razor blade held by a hemostat and a scalpel.
Slice along the edge of the razor blade with the scalpel multiple times in different directions until tissue is finely minced.
Add 10-20 mL of warm Collagenase to the dish containing minced dermal pieces.
Collect the Collagenase solution and minced dermal pieces using a 50 mL serological pipet.
Transfer the mixture to a 50 mL conical tube, recovering as much of the minced dermis from the dish as possible.
Agitate the tissue suspension by pipetting up and down for 1-2 minutes using a 50 mL serological pipet.
Incubate the tube with minced tissue in Collagenase at 37°C in a water bath for 30–120 minutes, depending on the thickness of the tissue.
Agitate the tissue every 15–30 min until it is sufficiently digested.
Clean the outside of the tube with 70% alcohol when moving from the water bath to the hood.
Reduce the size of the pipet from 50 mL to 25 mL as the tissue digests.
Centrifuge at 1000 rpm (∼250×g) for 7 min at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant with a 50 mL pipet.
Resuspend pellet in 30 mL FGM.
Repeat steps 7G and 7H.
Resuspend pellet in FGM using 5 mL of medium for each T150 flask.
Add cells to prepared flasks pre-equilibrated with 10 mL FGM.
Pipette the dermal cell suspension down the growth surface of the flask carefully.
Label the flasks with #1.
Place the flasks in the incubator overnight (∼16 h).
Incubate epidermal strips in pre-warmed trypsin/EDTA solution with agitation.
Coat a 25 mL serological pipette with KGM +10% FBS by pipetting up and down several times.
Agitate the epidermal strips for approximately 5 minutes using the coated pipette.
Add 20 mL KGM + 10% FBS to the epidermal strips in trypsin/EDTA to neutralize the enzyme.
Filter the cell suspension through a 70 μm cell strainer into a clean, sterile 50 mL conical tube using a coated 25 mL pipet.
Transfer the strained cell suspension to ice until ready to centrifuge.
Transfer the epidermal strips from the cell strainer to a fresh 50 mL tube containing 20 mL HBS using sterile forceps.
Agitate the epidermal strips with a pre-coated 25 mL pipet for ∼4–5 min to release additional keratinocytes.
Repeat filtration of epidermal strips through a 70 μm cell strainer into a fresh tube containing 20 mL KGM + 10% FBS.
Place the filtered solution on ice until ready to centrifuge.
Transfer the epidermal strips into a second tube containing 20 mL HBS and repeat agitation with a 25 mL pipet for 4–5 minutes.
Repeat filtration of the solution with epidermal strips using a 70 μm cell strainer into a new tube containing 20 mL KGM + 10% FBS.
Centrifuge all epidermal cell suspensions for 7 minutes at 1000 rpm (∼250×g) at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatants from all tubes by aspirating or pipetting, taking care not to disturb the pellets.
Resuspend the cell pellets in cold KGM (200 μM calcium chloride).
Combine the resuspended cells into a single tube or sterile bottle.
Remove an aliquot for counting.
Place the remaining cell suspension on ice until ready to inoculate flasks.
Dilute the cell suspension 1:10 and count using a hemacytometer.
Count viable, proliferative cells using a hemacytometer.
Inoculate into collagen-coated T225 flasks pre-equilibrated with 45 mL KGM at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Place flasks in incubator overnight (∼16 h).
Rinse flasks 2-3 times with 5 mL HBS to remove debris.
Replace flask contents with fresh ECGM, using 15 mL per T75 flask.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 48 hours before changing media again.
Set up 2 T150 flasks for fibroblast pieces and label as “#2” flasks.
Add 10 mL FGM to each flask and equilibrate in incubator for ∼30 min.
Collect media and floating tissue pieces from #1 flasks and transfer to a sterile 50 mL conical tube.
Replace with 25 mL fresh media per T150 flask and place #1 flasks back into the incubator.
Centrifuge collected tissue pieces at 1000 rpm (∼250×g) for 7 min at 4°C.
Carefully aspirate or pipet off supernatant (pellet will not be tight).
Resuspend tissue pieces in 5 mL FGM.
Inoculate half into each of the 2 T150 flasks prepared above.
Supplement a bottle of KGM-LC (“low calcium,” 0.06 mM CaCl2).
Change P0 keratinocytes into KGM-LC one day after inoculation.
Feed keratinocytes with 45 mL of KGM-LC per T225 flask until passaged to P1.
Monitor the appearance of dividing cells and small colonies from days 2–4.
Ensure the change to KGM-LC on culture day 1 for feeder-free primary cultures.
Change media every 48 hours using 15 mL ECGM/T75 flask until cells approach confluence.
Passage the cells before confluence is reached; target density is 85%–90% confluence.
Harvest the cells at lower density if significant fibroblast contamination is present.
Change medium to fresh FGM in all #1 and #2 flasks, 25 mL per T150 flask.
Continue to change using 25 mL FGM every 48 h until cells approach confluence.
Change medium 24 h prior to harvesting and passaging or cryopreserving cells.
Do not wait until fibroblasts are confluent to passage them.
Change medium every 48 hours for keratinocytes until they approach confluence.
Give one extra medium change the day before harvesting keratinocytes for passage to P1.
Observe melanocytes in epidermal keratinocyte cultures by culture days 2–3.
Remove melanocytes from flasks via differential trypsinization before keratinocytes exceed ∼50% confluence.
Passage fibroblasts when they are ∼90%–95% confluent.
Perform the separation procedure after keratinocyte colonies are visible and melanocytes can be seen in flasks, but before keratinocytes begin to approach confluence.
Use a 1:10 dilution of trypsin/EDTA solution when removing melanocytes from P0 keratinocytes.
Repeat the use of 1:10 dilution of trypsin/EDTA solution at subsequent passages to minimize contamination with keratinocytes.
Warm HBS in a 37°C water bath.
Warm MGM in a 37°C water bath.
Warm FBS in a 37°C water bath.
Warm KGM-LC in a 37°C water bath.
Mix 1 mL of 0.025% Trypsin + 0.02% EDTA with 9 mL HBS for each T225 flask to prepare trypsin/EDTA solution.
Store the diluted trypsin/EDTA solution on ice until use.
Warm the diluted trypsin/EDTA solution to 37°C immediately before use.
Mix 1 mL of FBS with 9 mL MGM for each T225 flask to prepare a 10% FBS “stop” solution.
Coat T75 flasks (1 per 1–3 T225 of keratinocytes) with 3 mL 100% FBS.
Rock the coated T75 flasks to cover entire growth surface evenly.
Incubate the coated T75 flasks at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Aspirate all the FBS from the coated T75 flasks.
Add 15 mL MGM to each T75 flask and pre-equilibrate in incubator before inoculating melanocytes after removal from keratinocytes.
Turn on centrifuge and pre-chill to 4°C.
Aspirate medium from keratinocyte flasks (T225s).
Add 10 mL HBS to each flask, gently rock to rinse cell surface, and incubate at room temperature for 3–4 minutes.
Aspirate HBS and repeat wash step once.
Add 10 mL diluted, warmed trypsin/EDTA to each T225 flask.
Rock very gently to ensure complete coverage of growth surface with trypsin/EDTA solution.
Incubate at room temperature for 3–4 minutes.
Quickly check under microscope; melanocytes should be releasing from flask but keratinocytes should not.
Check keratinocytes under the microscope during the procedure.
Collect diluted trypsin/EDTA solution containing melanocytes and add to a 50 mL conical tube containing 10% FBS.
Rinse each flask very gently with 10 mL HBS and check under microscope.
If keratinocytes are still tightly adhered, collect this HBS wash and add to the tube(s) with collected melanocytes.
If keratinocytes appear to be releasing from the flask, discard this wash solution.
Add 45 mL KGM-LC to each T225 with keratinocytes and place back in incubator.
Centrifuge tubes with melanocytes at 1000 rpm (∼250×g) for 7 min at 4°C.
Resuspend melanocyte pellet in MGM; remove aliquot for counting.
Inoculate melanocytes into pre-equilibrated FBS-coated flasks at ∼5 × 10^4/cm^2 and place in incubator.
Aspirate the medium from flasks containing isolated melanocytes.
Replace with fresh MGM.
Change medium to fresh MGM (15 mL/T75 flask) every 48 hours until melanocytes are ready to harvest for passage.
Repeat differential trypsinization on subsequent days if necessary, but do not repeat on the same day to avoid damaging keratinocyte yield.
Transfer melanocytes to fresh T75 flasks after at least 2–3 days if keratinocytes are present as contaminants in melanocyte cultures.
Culture keratinocytes in tissue culture-treated flasks without collagen coating for passages P1 and beyond.
Use medium containing 0.2 mM CaCl2 for culturing keratinocytes at P1 and beyond.
Subculture keratinocytes prior to reaching confluence to maintain colony forming efficiency and proliferative potential.
Do not allow the density of P0 keratinocytes to exceed that shown in Figure 3F.
Decontaminate tissue culture hood.
Prepare aspirating flask by adding bleach for decontamination.
Add 68.5 μL of 0.5M EDTA to 50 mL HBS to make a dilute EDTA solution.
Sterile filter the EDTA solution through a 0.22 μm tube top filter.
Warm HBS and KGM in a 37°C water bath.
Pre-chill centrifuge to 4°C.
Thaw 0.025% Trypsin + 0.02% EDTA on ice; warm just prior to use.
Prepare a “stop” solution consisting of 10% FBS in KGM and store on ice.
Remove flasks from incubator.
Aspirate KGM from flasks.
Add 10 mL HBS per flask and rock for 30 s–1 min.
Aspirate the HBS.
Add 10 mL dilute EDTA solution to each flask and rock to even coat growth surface.
Incubate at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 5 min.
Aspirate the dilute EDTA solution.
Add 5 mL warm trypsin/EDTA solution to each flask.
Place flasks in incubator at 37°C and incubate for 3–5 min.
Remove flasks from incubator.
Check under microscope to ensure cells are rounded up but still attached.
Gently tap flasks to loosen cells.
Rock flasks back and forth to further loosen cells.
Continue tapping and rocking until most cells have released from the surface.
Work quickly to avoid leaving cells in trypsin/EDTA solution for more than 5–6 min.
Check under microscope periodically during the process.
Collect cell suspension and add to tube(s) containing cold 10% FBS in KGM to neutralize the trypsin.
Add 10 mL HBS per flask to rinse; using a 10 mL pipet, spray the HBS rinse directly onto the growth surface several times to release any remaining cells.
Collect this rinse and add it to the tube(s) with trypsinized cells in 10% FBS solution.
Centrifuge at 1000 rpm (∼250×g) for 7 min at 4°C.
Resuspend cells in KGM and remove a small amount to count using a hemacytometer.
Keep keratinocytes on ice while counting and until ready to inoculate.
Inoculate keratinocytes at a density of 2–10 × 10^3/cm².
Monitor the cells for growth until they reach approximately 80%–90% confluence.
Harvest keratinocytes when near-confluence is reached, expecting to obtain ∼1 × 10^5 keratinocytes/cm² (∼22.5 × 10^6 per T225 flask).
For melanocytes and HDMEC, inoculate into flasks at a minimum density of 5,000/cm².
Coat flasks with Attachment Factor for HDMEC as described in step 4h.
Add ECGM to the coated flask(s) and equilibrate in an incubator.
For fibroblasts, no coating is needed; equilibrate the flask(s) with FGM in the incubator.
Harvest cells when they reach ∼90% confluence.
Rinse the flask briefly with HBS (5–10 mL) before adding trypsin.
Add 3 mL of 0.025% Trypsin + 0.02% EDTA for T150 flasks and 2 mL for T75 flasks.
Incubate cells in trypsin for ∼2–3 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Gently tap and rock the flask to dislodge cells after trypsin treatment.
Rinse flasks with HBS after trypsinization.
Add the rinse to the tube containing trypsinized cells.
Inoculate harvested cells into flasks as described for keratinocytes.
Do not inoculate HDMEC below 5,000/cm².
Fibroblasts should double every ∼16–20 hours.
Harvest melanocytes at ∼90% confluence.
Prepare 10% FBS in MGM for neutralizing trypsin during melanocyte harvest (≥1 mL per mL of trypsin).
Add MGM to flask(s) and equilibrate in incubator.
Use FBS-coated flasks for every passage of melanocytes.
Perform a brief HBS rinse prior to adding trypsin.
Treat with trypsin at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for ∼2–3 min to loosen and remove cells.
Rinse flasks with HBS after trypsinization and add the rinse to the tube(s) with trypsinized cells.
Centrifuge the trypsinized cells.
Resuspend the cells in medium after centrifugation.
Count the resuspended cells.
Inoculate into prepared FBS-coated, pre-equilibrated flasks at ≥5,000/cm².
Turn on cell freezer and pre-chill before use.
Harvest cells as detailed for each specific cell type.
Resuspend harvested cells in growth medium and store on ice.
Remove an aliquot of resuspended cells to count using a hemacytometer.
Calculate the total number of cells harvested based on the count.
Count cells prior to freezing to facilitate planning and predictable performance upon recovery.
Freeze 1–6 × 10^6 cells per vial in cryovials assuming a volume of 1.8 mL for each vial.
Pellet cells by centrifuging at 1000 rpm (∼250×g) for 7 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the medium and resuspend the cell pellet in cold freezing medium to yield the correct number of cells per 1.8 mL.
Calculate the required volume of freezing medium based on total cells counted using the formula: Total # cells counted × (mL total / # cells/vial) = mL/final vial.
Aliquot the resuspended cells into cryovials at 1.8 mL per vial for freezing.
Aliquot cells into freezing vials on ice.
Transfer freezing vials to a cell freezer for cryopreservation.
For fibroblasts, keratinocytes, and HDMEC, use a freezing rate of -10°C/min.
For melanocytes, particularly from darker skinned donors with high melanin content, use a slower freezing rate of -1°C/min.
If a controlled rate cell freezer is not available, use alternative methods such as Mr. Frosty™ for cryopreservation.
Transfer vials quickly to liquid nitrogen for storage.
Avoid any temperature increases during the transfer process to maintain cell viability.
